correctness.rationale: Conjugation averaging uses the full price-preserving graph automorphism group; SLEM is a convex spectral norm and edge cost is invariant and linear. Four exact invariant eigenvalues yield the linear-program constraints \(a\ge r/n\), \(b\ge[r-(n-2)a]/2\) and \(a\le2\theta/n\). The lower envelope has one kink and two slopes, separated by the explicit critical price. All three branches and the critical-price optimizer segment satisfy every remaining eigenvalue bound, stochastic diagonal and boundary for all \(n\ge3\) and \(\theta\in[1/3,1)\). Averaging any non-invariant competitor has equal cost and no worse SLEM. The budget formula follows by inverting the branch costs. The exact rational checker completed 12,885 finite assertions; these do not prove the infinite-family claim.

value.rationale: The edge-price distinction is a natural network design problem: \(n\) matched links compete economically with \(n(n-1)\) alternatives under a bound on contraction. The theorem gives a complete nontrivial two-phase resource Pareto law, a price boundary independent of contraction tolerance, a constraint threshold at which matching links are forced/discarded, and all symmetric optimizers at equality. Unlike solving one arbitrary SDP instance, the infinite family is classified with structural, exact engineering implications.
